question.problem:
Consider the matrix $B$ for which ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-6$ are eigenvalues, and

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

are the respective eigenvectors. What are the values of $a,b,c$ given that

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ b & c\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & a\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ b & c\end{aligned}]}^{-1}?
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-6,$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=4,$ and

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=-6.$

Therefore, we get

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & -6\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}.
$$

 

In conclusion, we get  $a=-6,$ $b=3,$ and $c=-1.$
